original.reason: The claimed result is correct, but the argument excluding primes q>3 is reversed: imposing p≡-1 (mod q) makes q divide p+1, rather than showing q does not divide every p+1. Thus it does not establish that the gcd is 6.

judgment.reason: For q≠2,3 it selects p≡-1 (mod q), which implies q|p+1, yet concludes q∤p+1. This reverses the needed implication and fails to exclude additional prime divisors.
The CRT/Dirichlet step chooses p≡-1 (mod q), so q divides p+1, contrary to its stated conclusion q∤p+1. Hence the proof that D divides 6 is incomplete.
Its final exclusion of primes q≠2,3 contains the same reversed congruence inference: p≡-1 (mod q) gives q|p+1, not q∤p+1.
The proof's key final step is false: for p≡-1 (mod q), one has q|p+1. Therefore it has not ruled out extra prime factors of D.
